question: How is a Skilled Worker's required salary adjusted if they work part-time, e.g. 30 hours a week instead of 37.5?
expected_answer: The going rate is pro-rated: going rate × (weekly hours ÷ 37.5)
model_answer:
The salary requirement is applied on a **pro‑rata** basis.  
You take the full‑time threshold (the amount required for a 37.5‑hour week) and scale it to the actual average weekly hours the worker will do.

**Formula**

\[
\text{Required annual salary for part‑time} =
\text{Full‑time threshold} \times \frac{\text{average weekly hours}}{37.5}
\]

So, for a 30‑hour‑per‑week role:

\[
\text{Required salary} = \text{Full‑time threshold} \times \frac{30}{37.5}
\]

In practice you can also calculate it directly as:

\[
\text{Required salary} = \text{Hourly rate} \times 30 \times 52
\]

provided the resulting annual figure meets the pro‑rated amount above. This ensures the salary meets the same proportion of the minimum as a full‑time worker would.
